stories.title: Woman arrested by gardaí investigating UCD deception
stories.summary: A woman has been arrested by gardaí investigating alleged deception against a third-level institution. The woman, who is in her 20s, is being detained under Section 4 of the Criminal Justice Act at a south Dublin garda station and can be questioned for up to 24 hours. Gardaí also carried out a search and seized a number of items including electronic devices as part of their investigation. It is understood she is being questioned in relation to allegedly fraudulent documentation supplied to UCD.

stories.title: Man, 30s, due to appear in court over Waterford stabbing
stories.summary: A man has been charged after a woman was stabbed at a church in Tramore, Co Waterford. The woman in her 50s was seriously injured during the incident at Holy Cross Church in Summerhill before 10am yesterday. She was taken to University Hospital Waterford with serious, but non-life-threatening injuries. The man, who is in his 30s, is due to appear before Waterford District Court later this morning.

stories.title: Govt set to publish Summer Economic Statement
stories.summary: The Government will publish details of the Summer Economic Statement later today, which will set out how much money the Coalition will have for tax cuts in the Budget in October. It is expected the room for taxation measures will be in the region of €1.5 billion. This will be on top of capital and current spending increases of about €7bn. The Coalition did not increase the point people pay the higher rate of tax this year.

stories.title: Zelensky dismisses army chief after days of protests
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has dismissed his Soviet-trained army chief Oleksandr Syrsky following a political crisis triggered by the removal of a popular, young and tech-savvy defence minister. Mr Zelensky announced he was appointing joint forces commander Mykhailo Drapaty in his place. Mr Syrsky, 60, had served in the role since 2024 and was among Kyiv's most experienced commanders, having led the defence of the city at the start of Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022. His removal came after days of protests in support of ousted defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov, who accused Mr Syrsky of forcing him out and stalling his attempt to reform the military.

stories.title: Bank of Ireland eyes economic growth of 3.5% for 2026
stories.summary:
Bank of Ireland has forecast that the domestic economy will expand by 3.5% this year and 2.5% in 2027. It also expects just under 40,000 homes will be built this year up from 36,000 completed last year. The bank says the measure of the economy which includes the multinational activity, Gross Domestic Product, will fall by 3% this year as the surge in pharmaceutical exports which was experienced in 2025 unwinds. It has revised downwards its forecast for inflation for this year as oil prices trade at around $90 per barrel down from their peak of almost $118 after the Iran war broke out.

Bank of Ireland says the phased withdrawal of Government supports means inflation will be 3.1% this year and 2.7% next year.

stories.title: Hosepipe ban extended as hot weather set to continue
stories.summary: Uisce Éireann is extending its hosepipe ban nationwide, bringing every county under water restrictions from just after midnight on Friday as Ireland's prolonged spell of hot, dry weather continues to put drinking water supplies under pressure. The six-week Water Conservation Order, which was introduced last week for the Greater Dublin Area and parts of Wexford, Wicklow, Meath, Kildare and south Tipperary, will now apply across the country until 26 August. It is one of the most extensive water conservation measures introduced by Uisce Éireann, with restrictions now applying nationwide as water sources come under increasing strain following an extended period of exceptionally warm and dry weather. The order applies to all households and prohibits the use of hosepipes for activities such as washing cars, watering gardens and filling paddling pools.

stories.title: New NI secretary Bryant vows open door to 'all parties'
stories.summary: The UK's new Northern Ireland Secretary Chris Bryant has said his door will be open to all the Stormont parties and all communities. Speaking after being appointed by new UKPrime Minister Andy Burnham last night, Mr Bryant said while daunting, and with a "heavy responsibility", he is "looking forward to getting properly stuck in". In a statement this evening, Mr Bryant said he was focused on maintaining political stability and promoting economic growth. "I want to be very clear from the outset: my door will be open to all parties and all communities," he said.

stories.title: Spain moves to ban smoking on terraces, beaches
stories.summary: Spain's minority left-wing government has approved a draft law that would ban smoking and vaping in outdoor spaces including bar terraces, parks and beaches. The draft law would also ban minors from consuming tobacco and prevent the advertising, promotion or sponsoring of tobacco products, which pose severe health risks including cancer. Health Minister Monica Garcia said the aim was to expand restrictions beyond an indoor smoking ban introduced in 2010 "to better protect public health and move towards a tobacco-free generation". "The aim is simple: to make clean air the norm in shared spaces," she told a news conference after the draft law was approved by the cabinet.
